title: Stop installing the obsolete SPI keyboard DKMS package
author: hudsonwa
body:
Fixes #9831

## What broke

`install/hardware/apple/fix-spi-keyboard.sh` installs `macbook12-spi-driver-dkms` on every MacBook it matches. That package is obsolete: `applespi` is mainlined (it ships in the `linux` package), and the out-of-tree copy includes `asm/unaligned.h`, which was removed in kernel 6.12. The DKMS build therefore fails on every kernel update once `linux-headers` is present (reproduced in the issue with the full build log). The failure is currently invisible on stock installs only because Arch's DKMS hook finds no `usr/lib/modules/*/build` without headers; issue #8285 proposes installing `linux-headers`, which would surface this failed build on every matched MacBook.

The keyboard itself is unaffected: the script also writes `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/macbook_spi_modules.conf`, which loads the in-tree `applespi` module into the initramfs. That half is load-bearing (LUKS passphrase entry), and the issue verifies removing only the package leaves the keyboard and touchpad working.

## Fix

Drop the `omarchy-pkg-add macbook12-spi-driver-dkms` line and keep everything else, with a comment recording why the package no longer belongs. The initramfs drop-in is unchanged, so initramfs behavior is identical.

## Why install/hardware

This is an install-time hardware leaf run via `run_logged` from `install/hardware/all.sh`. The package install belongs there (or nowhere), and the drop-in must stay there, so the fix is confined to the one file.

## Tests

New `test/shell.d/spi-keyboard-test.sh` runs a sandboxed copy of the leaf (DMI path and mkinitcpio dir rewritten, stubbed `omarchy-pkg-add`/`sudo`):

- Matched MacBook (MacBookPro14,1): the DKMS package is NOT requested, and the initramfs drop-in is still written with the SPI modules.
- Unmatched machine (MacBookPro15,2): nothing happens at all.

All pass here; the test fails against the pre-fix leaf (RED to GREEN). Honest host note: this machine cannot run a real pre-T2 MacBook, so the model regex is covered by the sandbox rather than hardware; the match set itself is unchanged.

## Not included

A migration that removes the package from already-installed machines was left out deliberately (machine-wide package removal is the maintainers' call; the script fix prevents new installs). Happy to add one if wanted. This also removes the regression #8285 would have surfaced.

@@ -3,7 +3,11 @@ product_name="$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name 2>/dev/null)"
 if [[ $product_name =~ MacBook[89],1|MacBook1[02],1|MacBookPro13,[123]|MacBookPro14,[123] ]]; then
   echo "Detected MacBook with SPI keyboard"
 
-  omarchy-pkg-add macbook12-spi-driver-dkms
+  # macbook12-spi-driver-dkms is obsolete: applespi is mainlined (it ships in
+  # the linux package, and its header that the out-of-tree copy needs was
+  # removed in 6.12), so the DKMS build fails on every kernel update once
+  # linux-headers is present. Only the initramfs drop-in below is needed to
+  # get the in-tree module into the initramfs (load-bearing for LUKS roots).
   sudo mkdir -p /etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d
   if [[ $product_name == "MacBook8,1" ]]; then
     echo "MODULES=(applespi spi_pxa2xx_platform spi_pxa2xx_pci)" | \

@@ -25,7 +25,6 @@ linux-firmware
 linux-headers
 linux-ptl
 linux-ptl-headers
-macbook12-spi-driver-dkms
 nvidia-580xx-dkms
 nvidia-dkms
 nvidia-open-dkms

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+echo "Remove the obsolete MacBook SPI keyboard DKMS package"
+
+# applespi is mainlined (it ships with the linux package), so the out-of-tree
+# driver cannot build on current kernels: its include was removed in kernel
+# 6.12 and the DKMS build fails on every kernel update once linux-headers is
+# present. The initramfs drop-in written by
+# install/hardware/apple/fix-spi-keyboard.sh loads the in-tree module instead,
+# so the package is pure failure surface. Idempotent: nothing happens when the
+# package is not installed.
+if omarchy-pkg-present macbook12-spi-driver-dkms; then
+  omarchy-pkg-drop macbook12-spi-driver-dkms
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,96 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT
+
+# The leaf reads /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name and writes under
+# /etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d, so a sandboxed copy with those paths rewritten is
+# used, like the other install/hardware tests.
+leaf="$tmp_dir/leaf.sh"
+sed -e "s|/sys/class/dmi/id/product_name|$tmp_dir/product_name|g" \
+  -e "s|/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d|$tmp_dir/mkinitcpio.conf.d|g" \
+  "$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-spi-keyboard.sh" >"$leaf"
+chmod +x "$leaf"
+
+mkdir -p "$tmp_dir/bin"
+cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/omarchy-pkg-add" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$PKG_ADD_LOG"
+EOF
+cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/sudo" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+exec "$@"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$tmp_dir/bin"/*
+
+run_leaf() {
+  printf '%s\n' "$1" >"$tmp_dir/product_name"
+  : >"$tmp_dir/pkg-add.log"
+  PKG_ADD_LOG="$tmp_dir/pkg-add.log" \
+    PATH="$tmp_dir/bin:$PATH" \
+    bash "$leaf"
+}
+
+# A matched MacBook: the initramfs drop-in has to keep the SPI modules (this
+# is what makes the keyboard work at the LUKS prompt), but the DKMS package is
+# obsolete — applespi is in-tree and the out-of-tree copy cannot build on
+# modern kernels — so it must not be installed anymore.
+run_leaf "MacBookPro14,1"
+[[ -s $tmp_dir/pkg-add.log ]] &&
+  fail "a matched MacBook no longer installs the obsolete DKMS package" \
+    "$(cat "$tmp_dir/pkg-add.log")"
+grep -q '^MODULES=(applespi intel_lpss_pci spi_pxa2xx_platform)$' \
+  "$tmp_dir/mkinitcpio.conf.d/macbook_spi_modules.conf" ||
+  fail "the SPI initramfs drop-in is still written" \
+    "$(cat "$tmp_dir/mkinitcpio.conf.d/macbook_spi_modules.conf" 2>/dev/null || echo missing)"
+pass "matched MacBook keeps the initramfs drop-in and skips the DKMS package"
+
+# An unmatched machine must be left completely alone.
+rm -rf "$tmp_dir/mkinitcpio.conf.d"
+run_leaf "MacBookPro15,2"
+[[ -s $tmp_dir/pkg-add.log ]] &&
+  fail "an unmatched machine does not install the DKMS package"
+[[ -e $tmp_dir/mkinitcpio.conf.d ]] &&
+  fail "an unmatched machine does not write the drop-in"
+pass "unmatched hardware is untouched"
+
+# Nothing installs the package now, so the ISO has no reason to cache it.
+! grep -qx 'macbook12-spi-driver-dkms' "$ROOT/install/omarchy-other.packages" ||
+  fail "the ISO no longer caches macbook12-spi-driver-dkms"
+pass "the obsolete DKMS package is gone from the ISO package cache list"
+
+# The install script no longer adds the package, but machines that ran the
+# old installer still carry one that fails to build on every kernel update
+# once linux-headers is present. The migration drops it idempotently,
+# following the tiny-dfr precedent.
+cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/omarchy-pkg-present" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+[[ -e $PKG_STATE ]] && [[ ${1:-} == macbook12-spi-driver-dkms ]]
+EOF
+cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/omarchy-pkg-drop" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$PKG_DROP_LOG"
+rm -f "$PKG_STATE"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$tmp_dir/bin/omarchy-pkg-present" "$tmp_dir/bin/omarchy-pkg-drop"
+
+migration="$ROOT/migrations/1788476400.sh"
+: >"$tmp_dir/pkg.installed"
+: >"$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log"
+PKG_STATE="$tmp_dir/pkg.installed" PKG_DROP_LOG="$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log" \
+  PATH="$tmp_dir/bin:$PATH" HOME="$tmp_dir" bash "$migration"
+grep -qx macbook12-spi-driver-dkms "$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log" ||
+  fail "the migration drops the obsolete DKMS package" \
+    "$(cat "$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log")"
+drops_before=$(wc -l <"$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log")
+PKG_STATE="$tmp_dir/pkg.installed" PKG_DROP_LOG="$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log" \
+  PATH="$tmp_dir/bin:$PATH" HOME="$tmp_dir" bash "$migration"
+(( $(wc -l <"$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log") == drops_before )) ||
+  fail "the migration only drops the package once" "$(cat "$tmp_dir/pkg-drop.log")"
+pass "installed machines get the obsolete DKMS package removed once"
+
+pass "SPI keyboard detection writes only the needed initramfs drop-in"

comments.body:
Reviewed by Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code, with an independent second opinion from Codex at xhigh reasoning. Tests ran on a disposable Omarchy 4.0.0 worker VM (kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2), never on the machine holding credentials.

The question that decides this one is what a matched MacBook uses for its keyboard and trackpad once the package is gone, and the in-tree path is there. On the worker:

```
$ modinfo applespi
filename:    /lib/modules/7.1.9-arch1-2/kernel/drivers/input/keyboard/applespi.ko.zst
description: MacBook(Pro) SPI Keyboard/Touchpad driver
alias:       acpi*:APP000D:*
$ pacman -Qo "$(modinfo -n applespi)"
... is owned by linux 7.1.9.arch1-2
```

One module for both the keyboard and the touchpad, shipped by the `linux` package, bound by the ACPI id rather than a model whitelist, so every model your regex matches is covered — and mainline has carried it since well before any kernel Omarchy has shipped. The initramfs drop-in you kept is what puts it in the initramfs for the LUKS prompt. No machine here is left without a keyboard.

The package also carried `apple-ibridge`/`apple-ib-tb` for the Touch Bar on MacBookPro13,2-3 and 14,2-3, which was never mainlined. Nothing is lost in practice: the build fails as a unit on 6.12 and later, so those modules are unavailable on any current kernel either way, and `manual/44-mac-support.md` already documents the T1 Touch Bar as non-functional.

Pushed one commit, `9605c7a`. `install/omarchy-other.packages` still listed `macbook12-spi-driver-dkms`, and per `docs/file-layout.md` the ISO builder reads that list for its offline mirror — so the ISO kept caching a package nothing installs. The T2 change did exactly this for `tiny-dfr` and `test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh:21` pins it; your test now carries the matching assertion.

Still open, and a decision for the maintainer rather than mine to push: removing the install line does not uninstall anything. Every MacBook that already ran the old installer keeps the package and keeps hitting the failed build the moment `linux-headers` arrives — which is the machine in #9831, and the regression #8285 would surface. `migrations/1785944594.sh:36-39` is the precedent for that half: an idempotent `omarchy-pkg-present` / `omarchy-pkg-drop` pair. As it stands this closes #9831 for new installs only.

Tests on the worker: `./test/cli` passes, and `test/shell.d/spi-keyboard-test.sh` and `test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh` pass. Your test is load-bearing — putting `omarchy-pkg-add macbook12-spi-driver-dkms` back makes it fail, and so does putting the package back in `omarchy-other.packages`.

Codex agreed with both points above, which I had already reached, so its independence is not currently guaranteed; it contributed the `docs/file-layout.md` pointer for what actually consumes the package list. It put applespi's mainlining at 4.11 and I have it at 5.3 — I verified neither against the kernel tree, and it changes nothing, since what matters is that the module ships in the kernel Omarchy runs today.

Thanks for the review and the ISO fix; caching a package nothing installs was the right catch. I completed the migration half: migrations/1788476400.sh drops macbook12-spi-driver-dkms idempotently when present, following the tiny-dfr precedent, so machines that ran the old installer stop hitting the failed build the moment linux-headers arrives. spi-keyboard-test.sh now covers the drop and its idempotence; the ISO assertion you added is in place.

Re-reviewed at `2d49be5e` by Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code, with an independent second opinion from Codex (gpt-5.6-sol) at xhigh reasoning. Everything executable ran on a fresh disposable Omarchy 4.0.0 worker VM, destroyed afterwards. Only the new commit is covered here; the earlier pass stands, and the ISO assertion is untouched.

**The migration is correct and I pushed nothing.** It is the half I left open last time, and the three things that could have made it dangerous all check out.

**No machine loses its keyboard at the LUKS prompt.** There has never been a released revision that installed the package without also writing the drop-in: `e018692e` (#1313) introduced both in the same conditional, at the same `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/macbook_spi_modules.conf` path it still uses, and every revision since kept them together. Removal is not silent about the initramfs either — `90-mkinitcpio-install.hook` triggers on `Operation = Remove` of `usr/src/*/dkms.conf`, which I read off the worker's own hook file, so the image is rebuilt inside the same pacman transaction and picks up the in-tree `applespi` the unchanged drop-in names.

**The migration actually reaches the machines in #9831.** `bin/omarchy-update:47-48` runs `omarchy-update-system-pkgs` before `omarchy-migrate` and both scripts run `set -e`, so a failed upgrade would take the migration with it — which would be the wrong outcome here, since the machines that need this are precisely the ones whose update hits the failed build. It does not happen: `main()` in Arch's `/usr/share/libalpm/scripts/dkms` collects failures into `ERROR_MESSAGES`, prints them, and ends with `return 0`. I read that on the worker rather than taking the warning text in the issue for it. The build failure is a warning, pacman's transaction succeeds, and the migration runs in the same `omarchy update`.

**`-Rns` takes nothing a MacBook needs.** On a stock 4.0.0 worker neither `dkms` nor `linux-headers` is installed — `install/omarchy-other.packages` is the ISO mirror manifest rather than an install list — so on an affected MacBook both arrived as dependencies of this package and `pacman -Rns` may take them back out. Nothing else on such a machine wants them, and the next correctly packaged DKMS driver pulls them in again.

Two notes, neither worth a commit:

- `AGENTS.md` says of `omarchy-pkg-present`: "don't use these if you can just use `omarchy-pkg-add`/`omarchy-pkg-drop`". `omarchy-pkg-drop:11-23` already filters to installed packages and no-ops otherwise, so `if omarchy-pkg-present …; then` is redundant here. The tiny-dfr precedent needs its guard because it runs `systemctl disable --now` first; this branch has nothing else in it.
- `docs/testing.md` and `bin/omarchy-migrate:93` both run a migration as `bash -euo pipefail`; `spi-keyboard-test.sh:85` and `:91` use plain `bash`. Nothing is hidden today — the migration has no pipeline and no unset variable, and a failing drop is still the script's non-zero result — but the strict form is what the runner does.

Tests, all on the worker: `./test/cli` green, `spi-keyboard-test.sh` and `t2-hardware-test.sh` green. The migration itself ran twice under `bash -euo pipefail` against a fake `HOME` on a machine that does not have the package, exit 0 both times — the real no-op path. Your new block is load-bearing: replacing the migration body with a bare `echo` makes the file fail at `not ok - the migration drops the obsolete DKMS package`.

Codex reviewed the same head at xhigh and found no defect, agreeing with conclusions I had already reached, so its independence is not currently guaranteed here — read-only sandboxing restricts writes and not reads. It contributed the mkinitcpio hook mechanism, which I had reasoned about wrongly and then checked on the worker. One claim of its I rejected: that `dkms` is installed independently by Omarchy via `install/omarchy-other.packages:10`. That file is the ISO manifest, and `pacman -Qi dkms` on a stock 4.0.0 worker reports it is not installed at all.

Two other open PRs edit `install/hardware/apple/fix-spi-keyboard.sh`, and one of them is a competing answer to this same question rather than a neighbour — that is the maintainer's call, not mine, so both are named here without a preference. **#10141** ("Stabilize MacBookPro13,3 hardware support") rewrites the same `omarchy-pkg-add` line, keeping the install behind a probe for an in-tree `applespi.ko` instead of dropping it; it adds no uninstall path, so machines that already have the package keep it. **#9735** ("Force SPI PIO on MacBook8,1") adds a block inside the `MacBook8,1` branch a few lines below and does not touch the package line, so it is a rebase rather than a conflict of substance; its migration `1788318101` sorts before yours, so ordering is fine either way.

Also related: #10154 does not interact with this. It is `install/hardware/intel/ptl-kernel.sh` on Dell XPS Panther Lake, and its bug is raw `pacman -Rdd` aborting on an uninstalled target — the failure mode `omarchy-pkg-drop` avoids by filtering to installed packages first.

Nothing pushed. Waiting on the maintainer, for how this sequences against #10141.
